messages:
anna: FYI ran a quick audit-scan and found keystore decrypts coming from a pod that shouldn't have access. looks like a hostPath-mounted token on init-container slipped through the admission policy.
jules: can you paste the audit line? need node + pod uid to trace.
anna: pasted: ```{
  "ts": "2026-03-04T02:14:08Z",
  "user": "system:serviceaccount:tenant:edge-proc",
  "verb": "keystore.decrypt",
  "pod_uid": "d4f8a2c3-7b1e-4e",
  "node": "onprem-node-12",
  "src_ip": "10.1.9.45"
}```
devin: that pod should not be able to talk to the keystore. how did it get a SA token on disk? which admission controller allowed hostPath?
rishi: the cluster recently migrated from PSP to PodSecurityAdmission in permissive mode for workloads labeled legacy=true. init containers using an older sidecar image mount hostPath:/var/run/secrets for convenience. we have an OPA constraint but it only covers new namespaces.
claire: immediate steps: 1) quarantine node onprem-node-12 (drain + cordon), 2) delete pod d4f8a2c3-7b1e-4e, 3) remove hostPath mounts from affected deployments, 4) revoke tokens for serviceaccount tenant:edge-proc, 5) apply a NetworkPolicy restricting keystore ingress to keystore-proxy and controlplane namespaces.
jules: add: disable external egress from tenant namespaces until we confirm no other exfil endpoints.
secops-bot: [alert] Detected keystore decrypt from unexpected namespace tenant at 2026-03-04T02:14:08Z. Ticket INC-2026-421 created.
anna: can someone run the audit query for all keystore.decrypt in the last 24h and correlate with pod_uid list? command I ran: ```kubectl --context=onprem-a logs -l component=audit -n kube-system | jq 'select(.verb=="keystore.decrypt")'```
devin: running now. also checking etcd audit retention snapshot to ensure we didn't miss older events.
rishi: policy note: we need an OPA gate that forbids hostPath mounts of "/var/run/secrets" and blocks init containers from mounting ServiceAccount tokens. i'll draft constraint.
claire: network policy snippet I'm applying to keystore namespace: ```apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-keystore
  namespace: secrets-store
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app.kubernetes.io/name: control-plane
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: keystore-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8321```
anna: Claire, deploy that and confirm curl from offending pod fails.
claire: applied. test from a repro pod in tenant ns -> curl 10.1.2.9:8321 returns Connection refused.
jules: revoke the tenant SA tokens and create a token-binding rotation. we need to ensure the HSM/WKM policy allows rewrap without requiring full customer approval. will ping compliance.
devin: forensic: found three distinct pods using same SA between 02:14 and 02:17. hostPath source: /var/run/secrets/tenant/token. node kubelet logs show cp /var/run/secrets -> /app/tok bind-mount.
rishi: put immediate guard: add mutating webhook that removes hostPath mounts referencing /var/run/secrets for non-system namespaces. also add admission failure for legacy=true label after 1h.
jules: for keystore integrity we should force rewrap of KEK and rotate envelope keys. but note: the keystore uses HSM with manual CMK (customer-managed) policy; rewrap API exists but will cause a brief rollover. Priya from Ops needs to coordinate.
anna: action items: (1) devin: full audit dump + etcd snapshot + kubelet logs (due in 30m), (2) claire: netpol + egress deny applied (done), (3) rishi: mutating webhook + OPA constraint PR, (4) jules: start CMK rewrap runbook and escalate to compliance if needed.
secops-bot: [update] INC-2026-421 assigned to eng-security oncall.
devin: posted S3 links with logs and correlated pod_uids. evidence shows no external outbound in that window except to internal keystore IP. no evidence of exfil to external endpoints.
jules: ops confirmed HSM supports automated rewrap via kms.rewrap(key_id) endpoint but customer CMK policy requires an access artifact. compliance says we can proceed under incident authority but must record artifact. I'll prepare the artifact request.
rishi: post-incident controls proposal: - enforce PodSecurityAdmission strict for legacy namespaces - OPA constraint to block hostPath /var/run/secrets - require SPIFFE workload identities for keystore access - keystore accept only mTLS from keystore-proxy with cert pinning - add keystore audit fields: envelope_key_id, pod_uid, node_ip.\lanna: (typo) anna: agreed on controls. also recommend removing clusterrolebinding tenant-support-admin that grants impersonation across namespaces; replace with per-namespace roles.
claire: confirm drained node has been inspected; no suspicious processes remain.
devin: revoked relevant tokens; pods that restarted now fail auth checks: ```kubectl auth can-i decrypt --as=system:serviceaccount:tenant:edge-proc``` -> "no"
jules: secops-bot, please close ticket when we've got PRs for OPA + webhook + RBAC tightens merged and HSM rewrap artifact attached.
secops-bot: [resolved] keystore unauthorized decrypts contained; INC-2026-421 status: mitigated. Next steps: postmortem and controls backlog created.
anna: we'll draft a short postmortem and link the artifacts. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
